task_title: Go installer: pinned toolchain under $HOME, module-resolution proof, provisioning hook for Go-kind projects
task_criteria: 1. scripts/install-go.sh --check/--apply installs a pinned Go toolchain under $HOME with no root and no system package manager, and reads the version back with the binary's own 'go version'
2. --apply proves the toolchain beyond --version: it resolves a pinned module through the node's own GOPROXY configuration with a cold module cache, or FAILs naming the proxy
3. A second --apply changes nothing, prints that it is already at the pinned version, and exits 0
4. --check FAILS (exit 1, a row beginning 'FAIL' that names go) on a fixture with no toolchain and no PATH entry, and PASSES on a host with the applied toolchain
5. Provisioning invokes install-go.sh only for kind sets that include go, and layer 10 --check names go as missing for those
6. tests/selftest.sh carries a new numbered section that exercises both the failing and the passing arm, so neither can regress silently
7. specs/NODE.md layer-10 text names the installer and the pinned version, because AGENTS.md makes the spec the design authority
